Customer targets: p95 <= 250ms for short chats (<=128 tokens) at 75 concurrent streaming connections, and sustained token/sec benchmarks for batch/rerank workloads. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, encryption/KMS, VPC peering, and benchmarking plan. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, run POC benchmarks, schedule infra deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-15 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Horizon CTO), Luis Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Anika Patel (Security)

Auto Summary: scope is latency and throughput across hosted/dedicated/private. Primary concerns: p95 targets, streaming latency, concurrency, token/sec for batch workloads, and security/compliance (KMS, VPC).

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intro, i'm jordan from redwood, this is priya our solutions eng, and we wanted to understand your latency/throughput goals and current infra.
[00:20] Maya (Horizon CTO): thanks jordan, on our side i'm maya, cto, luis is lead ml and anika is security. we run a real-time summarization API used in our product, latency is a big deal for us.
[00:35] Luis (Horizon): yeah we have 75 concurrent streaming connections in typical peak and need p95 around 200-300ms for short responses, longer context requests can be up to 1k tokens where p95 can be 800-1200ms.
[00:52] Priya (Redwood SE): okay that's helpful, can you give us current stack? are you on self-hosted gpus or cloud endpoints?
[01:05] Maya: currently mixed; prod is a managed endpoint from a cloud vendor for prototyping, but we've been experimenting with colocated 8xA100 hosts for lower variability and cost. we are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[01:22] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly the comparison many customers do. quick note: streaming adds a small constant overhead but also lets you start returning tokens earlier; the p95 for first-byte vs end-of-sentence varies. what p95 are you measuring today and how are you measuring it?
[01:40] Luis: we measure end-to-end with payloads and client-side timers. our short prompts are ~40-80 tokens and median is ~120ms but p95 spikes to 350ms sometimes. that's unacceptable.
[01:55] Priya: okay, so target is p95 <= 250ms for short forms?
[02:02] Maya: yeah that's ideal, we can tolerate higher for long runs but 75 concurrent streaming with that p95 is the must-have.
[02:12] Jordan: got it. a few clarifying q's: do you require strict data residency or KMS/HSM for keys? and will you need private control plane (air-gapped) or is VPC peering sufficient?
[02:25] Anika (Security): we need SOC 2 type II and customer-managed keys (KMS) for production; VPC peering is acceptable, private on-prem only for an eventual roadmap. also we need audit logs for every inference request.
[02:40] Priya: redwood supports SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, and per-token audit logs in our retention packages. private deployment supports customer-managed control plane and HSM.
[02:53] Anika: good, can you share SOC 2 and network diagrams?
[02:57] Jordan: yes we'll share those after the call. i'll include the security pack.

-- Topic: Latency architecture and tradeoffs --
[03:15] Priya: to the p95 and throughput: for streaming and low-latency workloads you usually want to push to a dedicated capacity pool or private deployment to avoid noisy neighbor and multi-tenant jitter. hosted can work if you accept higher variability or buy reserved capacity. what's your expected monthly token volume?
[03:35] Maya: rough estimate is 6M tokens/month to start, but with growth projection to 30M over the year.
[03:43] Jordan: that's in a range where dedicated reserved capacity often makes sense financially and for SLOs. for 75 concurrent streaming clients, what's your average token/sec per connection?
[03:55] Luis: typical realtime stream is 5-10 tokens/sec per connection. bursts go up to 25 tokens/sec.
[04:05] Priya: okay so 75 * 10 ~= 750 tokens/sec sustained, bursts up to ~1.8k tokens/sec. for an 8xA100 private cluster we can usually hit that with room for overhead depending on quantization / model size. which model do you plan to serve?
[04:20] Luis: we are evaluating an open LLM with 20B param variant, and also a distilled 7B for lower latency paths.
[04:28] Priya: that aligns: 7B on q4 quantization is great for sub-200ms p95 for short contexts on A100 with continuous batching and KV cache; 20B will be higher and may need more GPU or better kernels. streaming warmup is important to keep KV cache hot.

[04:45] Jordan: quick aside on benchmarking: we recommend measuring three profiles: cold first-token latency (no KV), steady-state streaming p95, and batch tokens/sec for reranking. our benchmark harness can run with your prompts.
[05:00] Maya: yes we'd like that. how long do benchmarks usually run?
[05:05] Priya: typically 24-72 hours to capture jitter and autoscale behavior; for dedicated/private we do 48-72h.

-- Technical deep dive (performance knobs) --
[05:30] Priya: some knobs: model quantization (4-bit/8-bit), kernel selection, compilation (optimizer passes), batch sizing, prefix KV caching, and routing. with streaming you often trade a bit of throughput to keep per-request latency low.
[05:47] Luis: are you doing continuous batching? our traffic is fairly bursty so batching helps cost but hurts single-request latency.
[05:54] Priya: yes continuous batching that respects latency SLOs; we can set per-route max batch windows and target p95. also we do adaptive batching with priority lanes for single-token short requests. this is part of Redwood Dedicated and Private tuning.
[06:10] Jordan: do you have a SLA p95 requirement for 99.9 uptime or a latency SLA?
[06:17] Maya: uptime SLA is important but latency SLO is our big gate\u2014if p95 gets above 300ms short form, product goes into degraded UX.

-- Security & Compliance --
[06:30] Anika: on logging, does Redwood store request payloads by default? and how's retention handled?
[06:38] Jordan: by default we don't persist customer inputs beyond retention policies; you can opt-in for logs. we support customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs. for private deployments you control the logs.
[06:52] Anika: good. are there certifications for on-prem package?
[06:55] Priya: private package itself runs under the customer's compliance umbrella; we provide guidance and our control plane meets SOC2. we'll send the cert attachments.

-- Benchmarks/Numbers discussed --
[07:10] Priya: ballpark numbers: for 7B quantized Q4 on A100, first-byte latency ~40-60ms, end-to-end for 40-80 tokens median ~80-120ms, p95 ~180-260ms at modest concurrency. for 20B you're looking at ~2-3x those latencies unless you scale GPUs or use optimized kernels.
[07:35] Luis: that matches our expectation but we want to see real-world with our prompts. what about tokens/sec batch for reranking? we need to do batch reranks of 1k requests at once, throughput matters.
[07:48] Priya: batch tokens/sec depends on model; a single 8xA100 can do tens to low hundreds of k tokens/sec for 7B depending on batch and quantization. 20B will be lower. we'll include sample bench numbers in the report.

[08:05] Jordan: also consider routing policy: route latency sensitive traffic to dedicated pools and cheaper batch traffic to shared hosted endpoints to optimize cost.

-- Customer constraints & timeline --
[08:20] Maya: timeline: pilot in 3 weeks, production in 3 months if POC goes well. stakeholders: product, infra, security. success criteria: p95 <=250ms for short streaming, stable at 75 concurrent, cost per 1M tokens below $X (we will share target).
[08:40] Jordan: perfect. that timeline is feasible, typical flow: pricing -> POC -> benchmark -> SOW -> pilot.

-- Typical objections/Tradeoffs --
[08:55] Luis: cost vs latency: we might accept a bit higher cost if it guarantees p95. hosted reserved capacity could be simpler but private offers more control.
[09:05] Priya: yep that's the tradeoff. Dedicated gives predictable performance and throughput with reserved commit; Private gives max isolation and control (KMS/HSM) but higher ops.

-- Questions from customer --
[09:20] Maya: can we burst to hosted from private if we run out of capacity?
[09:25] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports fallbacks between pools and model variants; we can implement auto-burst to hosted with policy rules.
[09:32] Anika: what's the audit latency on logs and how long are they retained?
[09:36] Priya: logs are near-real-time in the console; retention is configurable and we can integrate with your SIEM. we'll share retention options.

-- Mid-call status (timestamps continue) --
[10:00] Luis: also curious about cold-start behavior with KV cache; sometimes our clients see big p95 spikes after idle periods.
[10:10] Priya: that's expected; we recommend warm pools for streaming and keep-alive. we also offer prefix cache and synthetic warmers that replay typical prompts to keep caches hot.
[10:25] Maya: what's required network-wise for VPC peering?
[10:29] Jordan: standard peering, routes, and VPN or Direct Connect; we'll provide network diagrams and a checklist.

[11:00] Priya: for benchmarking we'll need sample prompts, concurrency profile, and a representative client simulator. we'll provide the harness but ask you to run it (or we can run in a scoped POC env).
[11:15] Maya: we'd prefer you run the benchmark in a dedicated POC environment with our prompts. we can provide access credentials.
[11:22] Jordan: ok we'll propose a POC plan: 48h dedicated run, 3 profiles (cold, steady streaming, batch throughput), and then a results sheet with latency and tokens/sec.

[12:00] Priya: question on model variants: are you open to a two-path approach (7B for low-latency, 20B for high-quality fallbacks)?
[12:08] Luis: yes we like that. we want automatic fallback if 7B output confidence is low.
[12:14] Priya: we can do confidence routing and rerank hybrid workflows.

-- Pricing & commercial --
[12:30] Jordan: pricing: hosted is pay-as-you-go with token rates, dedicated is reserved commit with lower unit costs and dedicated GPUs, private is license + ops. i'll send a spreadsheet with ballpark numbers and recommended committed capacity for 75 concurrent streams.
[12:47] Maya: great. also what's the minimum commit for dedicated?
[12:51] Jordan: depends on region and instance type; typically starting at a few racks (we'll include a recommended starting footprint).

-- Closing & Next Steps --
[13:10] Jordan: recap: we'll send pricing + SOW draft, SOC2 and network diagrams, and Priya will share benchmark harness. we'll draft a POC plan for a 48h run.
[13:22] Maya: sounds good. please include expected p95 baselines for the 7B quantized model in the deck.
[13:28] Priya: will do.
[13:30] Anika: i'll review security docs once you send.
[13:33] Jordan: thanks everybody. we'll follow up and schedule the infra deep dive for next week.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed sometimes as "K V cash"), product names sometimes incomplete. There are a few overlapping utterances (crosstalk) near the end when scheduling next steps.
